backbone: Inbox + Case file — a genuine hybrid, not a winner. The judges split two-two (case-file 34.3 vs task-first 34.5 summed across four reviews, a 0.2 dead heat) but all four converged on the same merge and all four rejected map-first as an architecture while wanting its map engineering. Half one is task-first's personal Home for every role: a place rather than a filter, grouped by the action you must take, where nothing vanishes silently and every row leads with the site ('District 7 · Los Angeles · Route 101 · PM 12.30') instead of three internal ids. Half two is case-file's object page: /incidents/:id becomes the only record page in the product, with the Assessment, technical form, evidence, site and history as five tabs — Overview · Who has it · Technical form · Photos & site · History — instead of destinations. Navigation collapses from seven sidebar entries to at most four per role (Home, Records with Incidents/Event Groups/Assessments segments, Map, and one role-specific fourth), rendering as a bottom bar on phones, an 80px labelled rail on iPads and a 256px sidebar on desktops. Every hand-off is a route-backed guided flow that is a full page on a phone and a dialog on a desktop from one implementation. No backend object, field, role or state transition is renamed.

keyDecisions: Backbone is a declared hybrid, not a winner: task-first's Inbox plus case-file's object page. The scores were a 34.5/34.3 dead heat and the four judges' recommendations were the same merge in different words.

Navigation is four destinations per role, not three. Case-file wanted Home/Incidents/Map with Event Groups as a filter; the new-user judge overruled its own preferred proposal because the coordinator's first decision at triage is an event decision and Event Group carries the brief's highest confusion rating. Records is one destination with Incidents · Event Groups · Assessments as segments.

The field judge's 'Records shrinks to Incidents + Event Groups' and the domain judge's 'give the chiefs an assessment-shaped office view' are both honoured: Assessments stays a Records segment with per-state counts and a longest-in-step sort, but selecting a row opens the case file's 'Who has it' tab. There is exactly one record detail surface in the product.

Route grammar: flat record URLs are kept. The engineering judge's objection to case-file's /incidents/:iid/assessment/:aid is technical and decisive — those routes cannot be statically redirected and would need an async resolver on every legacy and mobile deep link. /assessments/:id and /submissions/:id render the same case file entered on the right tab, via one in-page hop through incident_id.

Seven tabs cut to five by folding Report into Overview and Site into Photos, and relabelled by job ('Who has it', 'Technical form', 'Photos & site') because the domain judge is right that Assessment/Form is the app's worst vocabulary collision. On a phone: four visible plus More, never a horizontally scrolling tab strip.

Tailwind's stock breakpoints are kept and none are added. Task-first's remap would silently reinterpret 136 existing utilities across ~50 screens in one atomic release in a repo with no DOM tests in CI. Container queries carry all panel-internal layout instead.

iPad portrait (768) gets a stated, re-measured composition of its own — 80px labelled rail plus a single pane with drill-in and supporting content as a bottom sheet — because it is today the worst-served width in the app (577px nav card, then an 860px rail).
Two-pane compositions switch on at lg (1024), not xl, since the measured defect is that the sidebar appears at lg while every grid waits for xl.

Map-first is rejected as a backbone but its map rulebook is lifted verbatim and applied to the Map destination and every embedded map. Its layer-chip model is rejected outright (it makes the internal object model the primary control) and 'waiting on me' stays a place, not a toggleable chip.

Three backend items gate, not ten: the submit/review state sync in one transaction (B1), office-scoping the APPROVED finalize list (B2), and GET /incidents/{id}/case (B3). Everything else ships with progressive's honest interim — keep the limit:1000 fetches and label counts 'of loaded'.

66 working days, not 49-64. The engineering judge is right that every proposal omitted the same three costs: building the runtime feature flag (three of four rollback plans assumed one this repo lacks), the manual QA matrix implied by no component test harness (4 widths x 3 themes x 7 roles), and the cross-client label work into email templates and the mobile app.

Phase order puts the shell fix and the vocabulary module first (Phase 0 kills the 700px problem and the printed enums), then the hand-offs (Phase 1 unblocks the branch chief, the engineer's locked form and the admin firehose), then the case file, then the risky form phase behind the feature flag with a GISA data-dictionary parity checklist.

The web photo-upload interim is named in writing as a product decision, not left implicit: until the attachment endpoint is callable from the browser, every form and evidence surface says 'Photos are added in the ERIS mobile app'. Without it the engineer's first-day journey still fails exactly where it fails today.

Per-theme --brand-text / --good-text / --bad-text / --warn-text and --line-strong tokens are added with a build-time contrast report. Light-theme brand, good and bad measure ~3.0-4.0:1 and fail 4.5:1 for 11-13px badge text; none of the four proposals addressed it.

Three pieces of written, tested dead code are mounted rather than deleted: WorkflowTreeView plus getWorkflowTree become the case file's Progress rail, IncidentResolveDialog becomes /incidents/:id/resolve, and getSavedCrossSection / listProjectCrossSections become the Terrain 'Saved sections' list.

openQuestions: Does signing off an assessment close the incident? FINALIZED leaves it open until /incidents/{id}/resolve; if the policy should be auto-resolve, that is a one-line backend change that removes a step from every journey.
Can more than one assessment exist per incident? The case file assumes one; a re-assessment would need a selector on 'Who has it' and a branch in the progress rail.

Is the submission attachment endpoint callable from the browser origin today (CORS and presigning), or is that a backend task? Until it is, the engineer's first-day journey ends one step short on an iPad browser.
Event Group versus Project on mobile: change the mobile strings in the same release, or ship 'Event Group (formerly Project)' for one release?
The legacy REVIEWER account role grants no authority but unlocks mobile tabs: deprecate and migrate, or keep it with the explanatory empty state?
A district with no DISTRICT_COORDINATOR routing row strands reports UNASSIGNED with no notification. Should ERIS refuse the report, or notify a fallback, as well as surfacing it in System health?
Who may add a reviewer? Should the assigned engineer be able to propose one when review is blocked, or must they ask a chief?
Theme and density persist per browser, so on a shared field iPad the last person's choice wins. Move them to the user record?
How long should 'Recently done by me' stay? The plan uses 7 days; weekly reviewers may want 14 or 30.
Do we keep three themes? Each triples the contrast verification surface; dropping Coastal would measurably cut Phase 6.
Does GET /auth/me expose a last_sign_in_at the client can read, for the 60-day 'How your work flows' return path?

Nothing marks an incident urgent, so every queue sorts by age. If Caltrans wants a severity or emergency flag driving order, that is a backend field and a new chip, and it must be decided before Phase 1 sets the sort.
